ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence on politically exposed persons (PEPS), immediate family members and close associates; mandatory screening against United Nations Consolidated List, UK HM Treasury Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database, and Gibraltar Sanctions Regulations 2019; ongoing transaction monitoring under risk-based approach; sanctions screening systems must be implemented before forming bank relationships and repeated at least every 30 days with permanent record retention.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry (Registrar of Companies) – official online name-search and reservation portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be submitted in English/Latin script. Any proposed name in foreign script must be accompanied by a certified English transliteration and, if requested, a sworn translation. The name must not conflict with any registered name in Gibraltar, must not be misleading as to the activity or structure, and must satisfy the Registrar's Statutory Naming Rules 2019.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may submit a written administrative appeal to the Gibraltar Companies Registry within 21 calendar days, stating the basis for eligibility and, where applicable, furnishing a prior approval letter from the competent regulator (e.g., Gibraltar Financial Services Commission for regulated tokens). The Registrar must respond within 15 working days. A further appeal lies to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar within 28 days of the administrative response. The application may be amended and resubmitted; no separate appeal fee is charged.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are permitted only through a licensed corporate service provider that maintains a physical registered office address in Gibraltar and holds the ELP's statutory records at that address. For this marine insurance surveying business, a pure virtual address without local operational substance is disfavored; a nominal physical office or continued use of the licensed CSP's address will comply as the statutory registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated 10-15% probability in the first 18 months) for a standard ELP with a clean AML profile, domestic corporate position and regulated service provider. Risk of physical inspection increases to 35-40% if the name contains a regulated-token word or if the activity description references insurance underwriting.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for an Exempted Limited Partnership. The general partner must file a capital statement showing the initial contributed or committed capital. No escrow account or capital deposit is required by the Companies Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, in accordance with the Limited Partnerships Act 2016 and the Exempted Limited Partnership Agreement, that the initial capital commitments of all partners be approved as set out in Schedule 1, without issuance of shares, and be recorded in the capital contribution register.

RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office address at Suite 5, 57 Line Wall Road, Gibraltar be adopted and the Gibraltar Companies Registry be notified.

RESOLVED FURTHER that the proposed General Partner be authorised to register the partnership, open bank facilities, and obtain the Marine Insurance Surveyor Operating Licence from the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission.

RESOLVED FURTHER that any one authorising officer be empowered to execute all statutory forms, regulatory correspondence, and banking mandates on behalf of the partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and exempted status pre-clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry through the Gibraltar Tax and Companies Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Gibraltar Tax and Companies Portal, select Companies Registry, and submit an ELP name reservation application. Indicate Exempted Limited Partnership status, attach consents for restricted words if applicable, and designate the proposed registered office. Pay the name reservation fee and retain the reservation reference until registration.
required_dossiers: Completed ELP Name Reservation Form
Certified passport copy of the proposed General Partner or certified constitutional documents if corporate
Schedule of proposed partners and nationalities
Registered office consent letter from a Gibraltar-licensed service provider
Consent for any restricted business name word
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried as misleading or contains a restricted word, submit a revised name reservation with the required consent within 7 business days. The first resubmission is free of charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarisation of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public in Gibraltar, with subsequent registration at the Gibraltar Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Limited Partnership Agreement containing the partner identities, capital contribution schedule, exempted status stipulation, marine survey business purpose, and profit-sharing rules. Ensure all partners or their lawful attorneys execute before a Gibraltar notary. For a corporate general partner, require the certified board resolution and incumbency certificate. Attach the notarial certificate of execution.
required_dossiers: Draft Limited Partnership Agreement
Notarised and apostilled corporate certificate of incorporation of the General Partner if corporate
List of General Partner and Limited Partners with capital commitments
Registered office consent letter
Capital contribution schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies an execution irregularity, prepare corrected signature pages, re-execute in the presence of the notary, and file the corrected pages before the registration application is submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Exempted Limited Partnership with the Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry - Limited Partnerships Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form ELP-2 together with the notarised Limited Partnership Agreement, capital statement, registered office consent, and exempted status declaration. Ensure at least one General Partner and one Limited Partner are named. The Registry will examine compliance with the Limited Partnerships Act 2016 and, upon approval, issue the ELP Certificate of Registration.
required_dossiers: Form ELP-2 Application for Registration of an Exempted Limited Partnership
Notarised Limited Partnership Agreement
Statement of initial capital contributions
Consent of registered office provider
Register of General and Limited Partners
Exempted status election under the Income Tax regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry raises a query on the registered office or partner identity, submit a revised Form ELP-2 and corrected underlying documents within 5 business days or appoint a different Gibraltar-licensed registered office provider.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution and internal governance pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner in corporate capacity, with minutes filed at the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the General Partner's first board meeting or obtain a written resolution. Adopt the final Limited Partnership Agreement, ratify registration, approve the initial capital contribution schedule, confirm the registered office, appoint authorised signatories for banking, and delegate the filing of the statutory operating licence application with the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission.
required_dossiers: Final text of the First Board Resolution
Certificate of Registration of the Exempted Limited Partnership
Registered office appointment letter
Authorised signatory specimen signatures
AML/CFT categorisation memorandum
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the regulator or bank insists on certified original minutes, reissue the resolution in original form, have the notary certify a conformed copy, and resubmit within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Marine Insurance Surveyor Statutory Operating Licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission - Authorisations Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the GFSC licensing application for Class M-2 Ancillary Marine Claims Surveying. Provide a programme of operations, fit-and-proper declarations for the responsible surveyors and compliance officer, AML/CFT controls, professional indemnity cover, and the company governance chart. Pay the required application fee and respond to any fit-and-proper assessment interviews.
required_dossiers: GFSC Marine Insurance Surveyor Operating Licence application form
Fit-and-proper questionnaire for General Partner, directors, and senior officers
AML/CFT policy and business risk assessment
Marine surveying operational plan
Professional indemnity insurance certificate
Organisational chart showing compliance reporting lines
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the GFSC issues a request for information, provide a complete written response and, where needed, amended business plan within 10 business days. The application remains pending until all fit-and-proper and AML queries are resolved; no automatic rejection occurs.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental and physical premises clearance for office-based survey operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of the Environment, Sustainability and Heritage; HM Fire and Civil Defence Service; Gibraltar Building Control Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange a pre-commencement inspection of the registered office and any storage premises. File an environmental activity registration confirming there is no industrial discharge. Obtain the fire safety clearance certificate for office occupancy. Submit a structural load letter and confirm compliance with workplace health and safety requirements for marine site visits.
required_dossiers: Environmental activity registration form
Fire risk assessment and means of escape drawings
Structural load letter from a qualified building engineer
Employer's liability insurance certificate
Health and safety policy and risk register for on-board survey work
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire or occupational inspection identifies deficiencies, remedy the stated defects within 14 days and request a reinspection. The corporate registration and licensing application are not prejudiced by physical clearance remediation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission - Authorisations Unit, coordinated with HM Fire and Civil Defence Service for premises clearance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Marine Insurance Surveyor Operating Licence (Class M-2 - Ancillary Marine Claims Surveying)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Sustainability and Heritage, HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 - Registration-only; no separate Environmental Impact Assessment report required for a non-industrial office and shipboard inspection base
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater discharge from the office; no VOC or stack emissions arising from survey services; any shipboard survey activity must comply with MARPOL Annex I and II prohibitions on ballast and oil residue release; waste handling, storage, and disposal must comply with the Gibraltar Waste Management Regulations 2011.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate under the Fire Safety Act 2013 issued after inspection by HM Fire and Civil Defence Service; structural safety clearance from the Gibraltar Building Control Authority; occupational workplace clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2018, including personal protective equipment requirements for marine survey activities at quayside and onboard vessels.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar - Income Tax Office (Commissioner of Income Tax) under the Income Tax Act 2010 and Taxes (Administration) Act; Registrar of Companies (Gibraltar Companies Registry) for ELP formation; HM Customs & Excise Department for customs and excise matters. Primary portals: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi and the Income Tax Office e-services portal; the Companies Registry online filing system for annual statements and statutory filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Exempted Limited Partnership (ELP) with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies under the Limited Partnerships Act 2020, filing the Statement of Particulars (name, registered office in Gibraltar, general partner details, exempt status election) and receiving a Companies Registry registration number. Step 2: File the ELP's particulars with the Income Tax Office and appoint a resident principal/finance officer; the Income Tax Office issues an Income Tax Reference Number covering all partnership and partner filings. Step 3: If the ELP imports or exports dutiable goods, register separately with HM Customs & Excise as a declarant to obtain a customs account/declaration ID. Step 4: No VAT identification number is required because Gibraltar levies no general VAT/GST. Step 5: For banking onboarding with underwriter wire or Wise payment rails, the Gibraltar-licensed bank will request the Companies Registry certificate, the ELP registration confirmation, and a CRS/FATCA self-certification for each partner in lieu of a domestic TIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; Territorial_Scope; Tax_Exempt_Zone. Under Part XXII Income Tax Act 2010, an ELP is fiscally transparent: each partner is assessed on their proportionate share of Gibraltar-source income. Non-resident partners deriving no Gibraltar-source income have no Gibraltar tax liability. A non-resident ELP may obtain 'exempt' status, placing it in the Tax_Exempt_Zone category with respect to income arising outside Gibraltar.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box regime. Statutory elections include: (i) an election under s.15 Income Tax Act 2010 for the ELP to be assessed as a company where all partners are non-resident, providing corporate-rate certainty; (ii) an exempt-ELP status election filed with the Registrar, requiring an annual declaration of non-residence and absence of Gibraltar-source income; (iii) a transparent-treatment election obliging partners to file Form T1 schedules including their distributive share; (iv) hybrid mismatch declarations under Gibraltar's OECD BEPS Action 2 implementation, notifying the Income Tax Office of any deduction/non-inclusion mismatches and any UK/HMRC coordination; and (v), for multinational groups, elections regarding the Pillar Two Income Inclusion Rule and Undertaxed Profits Rule as adopted in Gibraltar's Taxation (International Tax Compliance) framework.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No general VAT/GST or sales and use tax in Gibraltar, which is outside the EU VAT area; indirect taxation is limited to customs and excise duties under the Import Duties Act 2020 and Customs and Excise Acts (e.g., alcohol, tobacco, hydrocarbon oils). Marine insurance surveying services exported to foreign underwriters are outside the Gibraltar indirect tax base.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable - no VAT/GST is in force and no economic turnover threshold triggers indirect tax registration in Gibraltar. For customs purposes, any importer/exporter of controlled or excisable goods must register with HM Customs & Excise as an approved declarant; there is no minimum turnover threshold. The Gibraltar pound (GI£) is at parity with GBP.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance API, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping regime applies in Gibraltar for services. Electronic customs declarations (SAD/C88) must be filed through HM Customs & Excise's computerised clearance system before goods are released; no operator/API e-invoicing mandate applies to B2B marine surveying supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Gibraltar has no VAT/GST, so no 0% export VAT rating applies; marine hull and cargo damage survey services rendered to non-resident underwriters fall outside Gibraltar indirect taxation entirely, and the income is not subject to Gibraltar income tax unless attributable to a Gibraltar permanent establishment or source. For goods physically exported from Gibraltar, zero customs duty applies under the Import Duties Act 2020, provided the export declaration is filed and the goods exit the jurisdiction within statutory limits. Substantiation requires documentary proof that the principal is non-resident, the engagement relates to an insured vessel/cargo with a foreign insured risk, and the consideration is not borne by a Gibraltar-resident establishment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic SAD/C88 filing accepted by HM Customs & Excise) for goods movements
Bill of Lading or equivalent ocean transport document evidencing the voyage, cargo, and final discharge port
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/Wise transfer advice showing the foreign underwriter's remittance in a foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under the Income Tax Act 2010, incorrect or fraudulent partnership returns attract interest at the statutory rate plus a penalty of up to 100% of the under-assessed tax; the extended assessment window is six years for neglect and unlimited for fraud. False claims of exempt-ELP or non-residence status permit the Commissioner to withdraw exempt status, claw back Gibraltar-source income for the full extended period, and impose daily penalties for non-filing. Abusive zero-rating or customs export misdeclaration is prosecutable under the Customs and Excise Acts with seizure of goods, a civil penalty of up to three times the goods' value or GI£3,000, and imprisonment up to two years. In addition, the UK-Gibraltar Exchange of Notes and automatic exchange of information protocol allows HMRC to receive details of the ELP and partners, exposing parallel UK anti-avoidance reviews and Potential Pillar Two adjustable measures for groups in scope.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) — the prudential and conduct regulator for all licensed banks and financial services in Gibraltar. There is no separate Gibraltar central bank; monetary issuance of the Gibraltar pound (GIP) rests with HM Government of Gibraltar through the Commissioner of Currency, while monetary stability is anchored by the Bank of England through the sterling parity arrangement (GIP pegged 1:1 to GBP). UK HM Treasury sanctions and AML frameworks apply to Gibraltar as a British Overseas Territory, with local implementation by the GFSC and the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit (GFIU).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital account. Gibraltar maintains no exchange-control legislation, no prior-approval requirement for capital inflows or outflows, and no restriction on profit remittance or capital repatriation for an Exempted Limited Partnership. The GIP is freely exchangeable with GBP at parity, and multi-currency USD/EUR balances are routinely available. Practical friction is limited to correspondent-bank clearing for USD and enhanced due diligence on the ultimate beneficial owners; there is no regulatory FX rationing, no repatriation tax, and no withholding tax on ELP distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Gibraltar law imposes no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender obligation with respect to export receipts. Marine surveying fees may be retained in any freely convertible currency. The only binding disciplines are the record-keeping and suspicious-transaction reporting requirements of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015, and the obligation to ensure that receipts reconcile to the underlying survey contract and commercial invoice.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility — Wise (the Target payment rail; an FCA-authorised Electronic Money Institution, FRN 900510) onboards Gibraltar-registered ELPs fully remotely. Legal constraints: Wise is not a bank, does not lend, and client funds are safeguarded in segregated accounts under the Electronic Money Regulations 2011 without deposit-insurance cover. The ELP must pass beneficial-ownership verification and Wise prohibits sanctioned marine counterparties. Wise Business supplies a UK sort code, EU IBAN, and multi-currency balances (GBP/EUR/USD) with local ACH, FPS, and SEPA clearing, which is operationally optimal for a Low_Risk_Standard marine surveying fee-collection profile.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate requires directors to appear physically, but Gibraltar-licensed banks normally require an in-person or video interview for the ELP's authorised signatories and the General Partner's directors. Remote opening is accepted where a GFSC-licensed trust and company service provider certifies the identity chain and the source-of-wealth documentation under the Financial Services (KYC) Regulations. The Wise route is fully remote with no branch visit. A filmed interview may be imposed at the discretion of the bank's Money Laundering Reporting Officer for offshore-linked ELPs; documentary certification by a Gibraltar Notary Public or licensed TCSP mitigates this requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore parentage: ELP ultimately linked to a Cayman Islands exempted entity, raising economic-substance and beneficial-ownership transparency concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Gibraltar registered-office and physical-presence evidence; ELP partnership agreement and statutory register of partners; beneficial-ownership filing under the Gibraltar Limited Partnerships Act 2020; complete BO chain from the General Partner to each limited partner; licensed TCSP attestation; 12-month source-of-funds statements; prior bank references; notarised declarations of source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and war-risk exposure: marine hull/cargo survey instructions may involve vessels, owners, charterers, or cargoes on OFAC, HMT, or UN sanction lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written sanctions-compliance policy; daily screening logs against the HMT Consolidated List, OFAC SDN list, and GFIU guidance; contractual no-sanctioned-party warranty in every survey engagement letter; P&I club screening confirmation; IMO/vessel-identity verification records; absolute exclusion of Russia, Belarus, Iran, Syria, and Crimea-zone instruction channels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulated-activity drift: claims-inspection work may be classified as insurance distribution or claims handling, which requires GFSC authorisation or registration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GFSC confirmation or exemption letter under the Financial Services Act 2019 and the Insurance Distribution Act 2018, evidencing that the surveyor's mandate is confined to factual physical hull/cargo inspection and condition reporting; professional-indemnity certificate with a minimum of £1 million per claim; fully executed survey terms disclaiming claims-handling, premium-handling, and settlement authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of capital injection: inbound funding from the Cayman/UK upper tier triggers unusual-source or higher-risk-jurisdiction queries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call notices and subscription agreements; auditor-confirmed capital verification; 12-month bank statements of the remitting entity; tax-clearance and FATCA/CRS self-certification; full corporate-resolution chain; GFIU-compliant source-of-wealth form; bank-reference letter from the remitting institution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: remit from the Cayman/UK upper tier via SWIFT MT103 (with a UETR) to the ELP's Gibraltar bank account, using ISO 20022 purpose code EQUI (equity capital) or CFIN for intercompany funding, and remittance reference 'KY_ELP capital injection / marine survey venture'. The remitter name must match the LP subscription schedule. Deliver the executed capital-call resolution, subscription agreement, and beneficial-ownership register to the receiving bank before credit; expect a standard 5-business-day AML quarantine. For GBP wires use CHAPS or FPS through the bank's UK clearing sort code; for EUR use SEPA or TARGET2; for USD route via the bank's US correspondent. No GFSC prior approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 (with UETR) using purpose codes TRDP (trade in services), INSU (insurance premium), or CLAI (insurance claims) for underwriter, P&I club, and shipyard repair-cost settlements. Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700/MT707) and standby LCs (MT760) are permissible for reinsurance cessions or security obligations but are not standard for professional-service fees. For low-value European supplier and subcontractor payments use Wise Business local rails (FPS/SEPA/ACH); for same-day GBP use CHAPS. Every outbound payment must reference the survey contract number and include full payer identity to preserve a clear audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable GBP/USD and GBP/EUR FX forwards with Gibraltar International Bank or Trusted Novus Bank, tenors up to 12 months.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic crosses (e.g., GIP/CHF or GIP/JPY) executed via a UK-authorised dealer where GIP spot liquidity is insufficient.
Cross-currency swaps (GBP/EUR, GBP/USD) matching long-dated hull reinsurance claim liabilities, with EMIR reporting required if the ELP exceeds the non-financial counterparty clearing threshold.
Zero-cost collar FX options protecting annual EUR/USD survey fee income against GBP volatility.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the Limited Partnership (Form LP-AR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 42 days after the anniversary of the partnership’s registration date (calendar anniversary rule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of GIP 100 per day, capped at GIP 1,000; non-compliance for 6 months triggers automatic strike-off of the partnership.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Re-affirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership Register (administered by the Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within 14 days following the anniversary of registration; also within 14 days of any ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties under the Companies Act 2014 (s.450A): fine up to GIP 100,000 and/or 2 years’ imprisonment for the defaulting General Partner or MLRO.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year ending 31 December; filed by 30 November of the following year (e.g., FY2024 return due 30 November 2025)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalty GIP 100 for late filing; daily penalty up to GIP 3,000; at-risk assessment by the Commissioner in cases of continued default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Licence Annual Renewal (Category B – Professional Services)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Business Licence Authority (Ministry of Business)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal period 1 January to 31 March for the licence year commencing 1 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs double fee; operating without a valid licence is an offence carrying a fine up to GIP 10,000 and possible cessation order.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory independent statutory audit if two or more of the following thresholds are exceeded for the financial year: turnover over GIP 10.0 million (USD 12.7 million), total assets over GIP 5.0 million (USD 6.4 million), or more than 50 employees. A marine insurance surveyor falling below these thresholds may claim audit exemption; however, if the partnership obtains a licence from the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (for ancillary insurance services), a full audit is mandatory regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the EU (UK-adopted IFRS post-Brexit) for larger and licensed entities; FRS 102 (Section 1A) is permitted for small partnerships.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Gibraltar’s Beneficial Ownership (Companies) Regulations 2018, the General Partner must ensure that the partnership’s beneficial ownership register is updated and an annual confirmation statement is submitted to the Registrar of Beneficial Owners within 14 days after each annual anniversary of the partnership’s registration. The confirmation must re-affirm that the information is accurate, and any changes in the beneficial owners (including changes in general partner owned vehicles) must be filed within 14 days of the event.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (separate sections for General Partners and Limited Partners)
Register of Directors (for any corporate General Partner, kept at its registered office)
Minute Book of Partnership Decision (Written Resolutions and General Partner Meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – USD 2,800 per year depending on board and AML support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 10,000 for a small to mid-sized offshore partnership; high risk or complex structures may exceed.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (Gibraltar companies and partnerships are taxed at a standard corporate income tax rate of 0% under Gibraltar's Income Tax Act 2010, as amended; no branch profits tax is levied on non-resident entities carrying on business through a Gibraltar permanent establishment unless distributed as dividends to a Gibraltar corporate shareholder).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory corporate tax holidays or preferential deductions exist for marine insurance surveyors in Gibraltar because the headline rate is already 0%. However, a flat rate tax election applies to certain utilities (not relevant to ISIC 5222), and general deductible expenses under normal tax principles are available only to the extent a taxable profit would otherwise arise, which is not the case at the 0% rate. Non-resident partners of an Exempted Limited Partnership are not chargeable to Gibraltar income tax on profits derived from offshore or exempt activities, and no payroll tax or social security contributions are imposed on non-resident partners.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Income Tax Return on Form GTO (Tax Return for Companies and Other Persons) filed through Her Majesty's Government of Gibraltar Income Tax Office (ITO) electronic filing system; the return is filed using the official paper form or the ITO's mandated electronic template for entities not covered by the Companies House CT return. Partnerships such as an Exempted Limited Partnership file an informational partnership return Form GTO-P showing each partner's share of profits or losses.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 months after the fiscal year-end (the three-month extension is available only to companies; the general filing deadline for partnerships is no later than 31 January following the year of assessment, but where accounting periods align with the calendar year the return is due by 31 December of the following year; the ITO also requires delivery of audited financial statements and the partnership schedule with the return).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name of the Exempted Limited Partnership and ELP registration number issued by the Gibraltar Registry of Limited Partnerships.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter exact legal name as registered under the Limited Partnerships Act 2010; provide the ELP number and indicate 'Exempted Limited Partnership' category.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address and tax residence address; for non-resident partners, the jurisdiction of tax residence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Gibraltar registered office address. Indicate each non-resident partner's jurisdiction of residence; do not claim Gibraltar tax residence unless the partnership is managed and controlled in Gibraltar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period start and end dates covered by the return (fiscal year end).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the ELP's agreed fiscal period; non-resident marine insurance surveyor activities must correspond to the actual period in which surveys and claims inspections were carried out.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross receipts from business activities; total marine survey fees, vessel hull and cargo damage inspection fees, and claims survey service income from underwriting clients.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all worldwide gross receipts allocable to the Gibraltar ELP. Where the ELP is transparent and non-resident partners are not subject to Gibraltar tax, still report gross income in the partnership return for information purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses directly attributable to the business: survey vessel charter costs, travel to ports, subcontract surveyor fees, marine insurance claim inspection costs, professional indemnity insurance premiums, and office overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses incurred for the production of income reported in Box 4. No deduction is allowed for partnership distributions to partners or for amounts attributable to non-Gibraltar activities unless connected to the ELP's trade.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net assessable profit or adjusted loss after deducting allowable expenses; reconcile with the audited profit and loss account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Because the ELP is pass-through eligible and is not liable to Gibraltar tax at entity level, compute net profit for information and allocate it to partners by percentage share. Losses are ring-fenced and may only be relieved against subsequent profits of the same trade within five years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership schedule: names, addresses, tax reference numbers, profit-sharing ratios, and allocated shares of assessable profits for each general and limited partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List each non-resident partner with their jurisdiction of tax residence and percentage allocation. Confirm whether a partner carries on business through a Gibraltar permanent establishment; if not, note the applicable DTA or Income Tax Act exemption from taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax withheld at source or tax paid on account, if any; claims for credit against any positive Gibraltar tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero where no Gibraltar tax liability arises. Where a non-resident partner is subject to Gibraltar tax because the ELP carries on a taxable activity in Gibraltar, attach supporting certificates and make relevant claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration by the ELP's general partner or authorised local representative, including date and signature.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The general partner or authorised signatory must sign the return and confirm that the information is complete and accurate. For non-resident general partners, the local resident agent in Gibraltar must countersign where required.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the Gibraltar tax return attracts a fixed penalty of £100; if the return is still outstanding after 30 days from the due date, a further penalty of £20 per day may be imposed up to a maximum of £300; persistent failure can trigger an additional penalty of up to 100% of any tax liability, and the ITO may apply default interest at 8% per annum on unpaid tax. Failure to keep proper records or submit audited financial statements can result in penalties up to £3,000 and disqualification of a local agent.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (Gibraltar does not impose a dividend withholding tax on distributions made by a Gibraltar company or partnership to residents or non-residents, and there is no Gibraltar withholding tax on partnership profit distributions or allocations to partners).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Gibraltar has no comprehensive double taxation agreement with the United Kingdom for corporate income tax purposes in the standard OECD format; it has limited agreements and arrangements in specific areas (e.g. exchange of information agreements, not full DTA tax relief). To invoke any available relief, the non-resident partner must obtain a Gibraltar Tax Information Exchange Network certificate of residence from the Income Tax Office, complete the relevant claim form attached to the return, and submit the foreign jurisdiction's tax authority confirmation of residence (TRC) as required. For reduced withholding or exemption on UK-source income, the entity must apply to HMRC under the UK-Gibraltar Tax Co-operation Agreement for specific taxes; however, because the Gibraltar ELP is transparent, the partners may directly invoke the UK-Gibraltar arrangement if they are UK residents by filing Form DT/Individual or Company with HMRC. In all cases, beneficial ownership and economic substance documentation must be provided within 30 days of the request; the approval cycle is generally 60–90 days.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: No statutory withholding tax on interest or royalties is imposed by Gibraltar on payments made to non-residents. On UK-source royalties and interest, the UK statutory rates are 20% for royalties and 20% for interest (bank interest is paid gross under the UK gross payment regime); the UK-Gibraltar arrangements may reduce UK withholding to 0% only where the beneficiary is the beneficial owner and the appropriate HMRC claim form is approved. For Spanish, Portuguese or other treaty counterparty source payments, the applicable treaty withholding rates apply at the source jurisdiction; typical rates are 4–10% for royalties and 10% for interest where a treaty exists, subject to OECD Model conformity. Payments of survey fees by a Gibraltar underwriter to a non-resident sub-surveyor are made gross because Gibraltar has no withholding mechanism.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No specific Gibraltar statutory transfer pricing threshold in local currency is prescribed under the Income Tax Act 2010; however, the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines apply to connected party transactions where the transaction exceeds GIP 250,000 in aggregate annually for local file preparation. A formal Local File and Master File are required where the Gibraltar entity or ELP has related party transactions above GIP 250,000 (approx. USD 335,000) and either (a) the Gibraltar operations carry on a taxable activity, or (b) the transactions involve a jurisdiction with a preferential tax regime. For an Exempted Limited Partnership carrying on marine insurance survey services with no Gibraltar tax liability, the ITO expects contemporaneous documentation in accordance with OECD BEPS Action 13 principles when cross-border transactions exceed GIP 1,000,000, even though penalties are only enforceable where a taxable profit is understated.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Gibraltar's Economic Substance regulations are found in the Taxes (Economic Substance) Regulations 2020 and apply to entities that carry on relevant activities, which include distribution and service centre businesses but not expressly marine survey services; nevertheless, a marine insurance surveying ELP that performs claims inspection and risk advisory services for group companies may be characterized as providing 'headquarters services' or 'service centre' activities, requiring economic substance in Gibraltar. The test requires that (a) the entity is directed and managed in Gibraltar, (b) core income-generating activities are performed in Gibraltar by adequate employees, (c) there is adequate physical presence and expenditure proportionate to the level of activity, and (d) records are kept of the substance analysis. For an Exempted Limited Partnership that is tax transparent with all partners outside Gibraltar, the substance assessment follows the partners' substance; however, if the ELP has a Gibraltar permanent establishment or files a return claiming full exemption for non-residents, it must nonetheless file an Economic Substance return annually to the Commissioner of Income Tax in Gibraltar. Failure to meet substance requirements triggers a £50,000 financial penalty, possible annual penalties of £50,000 for continued failure, and the Commissioner may make a notification to the Registrar to strike the entity off the register.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and deliberate suppression of taxable income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating marine survey fee income, omitting invoices issued to underwriters for hull or cargo damage inspection surveys, or misclassifying non-exempt Gibraltar-source income as offshore exempt income while physically carrying out surveys in Gibraltar waters or from a Gibraltar office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Gibraltar Income Tax Act 2010 and the Criminal Procedure Act, tax evasion is punishable upon conviction by a fine of up to £10,000 per offence and imprisonment for up to 7 years; the ITO may also determine tax on a best-of-judgment basis and add fines of up to 200% of the evaded tax, plus interest at 8% per annum. In addition, any false statement in a return can lead to a penalty not exceeding £5,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts in Gibraltar will pierce the corporate veil of an Exempted Limited Partnership where the general partner has acted fraudulently or used the partnership as a sham; the general partner and any participating limited partner who knowingly made false returns are jointly and severally liable for the full tax underpaid, interest, and penalties. The Comptroller may issue a certificate of unpaid tax which is enforceable personally, and the Supreme Court of Gibraltar may impose a travel prevention order against partners suspected of departing Gibraltar without settling liabilities, and imprisonment may be ordered for contempt or for directors of the general partner who fail to comply with a restoration or winding-up order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and economic substance violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Exempted Limited Partnership as a letterbox entity with no real presence in Gibraltar while invoicing marine insurance surveying services to underwriters, using a Gibraltar registered agent address only, and performing all survey work through sub-contractors in foreign jurisdictions without direction and management in Gibraltar.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Taxes (Economic Substance) Regulations 2020, the Commissioner may impose a financial penalty of £50,000 for failure to meet the economic substance test, plus £50,000 for each successive period of non-compliance, and may initiate a strike-off under the Limited Partnerships Act 2010 or Companies Act regulations. If the ELP is considered to have misleadingly claimed exempt status, the ITO may assess profits on the taxable basis of a Gibraltar-resident partnership and impose a penalty of up to 100% of the tax that would have been due. The Registrar may also strike the partnership from the register, freezing its ability to issue legally effective survey reports or to hold insurance contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and its directors are personally liable for economic substance penalties if they signed the annual substance declaration knowing it to be false; the Supreme Court may order disqualification of directors for up to 15 years, require personal restitution of any fees or distributions received, and issue a certificate to the Financial Intelligence Unit for money laundering proceedings where the shell structure was used to disguise the location of value.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Carrying on marine insurance claim surveying as an unlicensed insurance intermediary without registration under the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC); accepting and disbursing underwriter wire settlements through the ELP bank account without appropriate client money handling controls; failing to conduct due diligence on the beneficial owners receiving claim survey payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Financial Services Act 2019, carrying on a regulated activity without a licence is a criminal offence punishable by a fine not exceeding £200,000 and/or imprisonment up to 2 years. The GFSC may impose a public statement, financial penalty of up to £500,000 for serious AML failings, and require an independent audit under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015. Each transaction processed without AML clearance may be treated as a separate offence, and the court may order confiscation of the proceeds under the Proceeds of Crime Act, including the full fees collected from marine insurers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior management and general partners who consent to, or connive in, unlicensed activity or AML contraventions are personally criminally liable and may be imprisoned for up to 2 years; the GFSC may issue prohibition orders banning them from any financial services role for up to 10 years; civil liability may extend to restitution to insurers for losses caused by negligent survey reports issued without regulatory oversight.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Inaccurate filing and failure to maintain records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the Gibraltar partnership return within the statutory 12-month period or failing to keep contemporaneous records of marine survey appraisals, fee invoices, and expense documentation for 6 years, causing the ITO to be unable to verify the exempt status of the ELP's income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ITO may assess the ELP on a deemed profit basis at the standard company rate where the ELP would otherwise be taxable, impose a late filing penalty of £100 plus daily penalties up to £300, and where records are inadequate the penalty is up to £3,000 plus an additional £50 per day for continuing failure. Interest at 8% per annum is imposed on any resulting tax from the date the tax should have been paid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner is personally liable for penalties to the extent the failure results from the general partner's default; if the record-keeping failure materially impedes a tax investigation, the court may order the disqualification of the general partner and grant a freezing injunction over personal assets; in aggravated cases of deliberate concealment, directors may face a term of imprisonment up to 2 years.
